svg.title: Agentic patterns under an untrusted runtime
svg.desc: One card per published agentic pattern. Plain nodes are the pattern as the field publishes it; filled nodes exist only because the runtime is untrusted. Lanes are UML activity partitions. The dashed red edge is the deny path the published diagrams have nowhere to show.
svg.text: Agentic patterns under an untrusted runtime
The pattern as the field publishes it, and what the trust boundary inserts into it.
NOT AUTHORITATIVE — design/intent/. States intent, never what is built.
Plain node = published pattern. Filled node = inserted because the runtime is untrusted. Dashed red = the deny path published diagrams omit.
Reason → request → decide → act → observe → respond
Anthropic: agents · OpenAI: single-agent loop with tools
The tool call is a REQUEST, never an action. The loop names an object; the kernel decides, and the subject's own descriptor is
Anthropic: routing · OpenAI: classify then dispatch
The classifier may PROPOSE a destination; it cannot grant one. An absent or empty allowlist refuses every role, so routing is
Generate → evaluate → revise until the output passes
Anthropic: evaluator-optimiser · the reel's Reflection / Critic
The field lets the model grade itself. Maknae's critic is an ORACLE the model cannot influence — a gate that must be observed
FAILING before it is trusted to pass.
CANDIDATE, not decided. Delegation transmits intent, never authority: the child is decided as if the user typed the task, on its
OWN conduit, and the return hop is a release decision. Neither loop's grant bounds the other's.
Agent A → transfers control → Agent B owns the conversation
OpenAI: handoffs — execution transfers to the receiving agent
A GAP, not a decision. Upstream's own contract: input guardrails apply to the FIRST agent only, output guardrails to the LAST.
Everything between runs unguarded — the failure this architecture exists to prevent.
